plan: Sell all leveraged ETFs like SOXL and SPAL to zero for capital preservation.
Exit weak positions such as METU, MUU, and PLTU that are below their stops.

conservative.read: This conservative approach targets around 1.5% per month, prioritizing capital preservation. It significantly reduces risk by eliminating leveraged ETFs and trimming concentrated positions. Expect lower drawdowns but also more modest growth potential.

plan: Trim SOXL and SPAL to small allocations (2% and 1%) to reduce leverage.
Reduce METU, MUU, and PLTU to small allocations (3%, 1%, 1%) to manage risk.
Trim SPY to 25% to meet the single-name concentration mandate.
Buy TZA at 4% as a new long setup from the scanner.
This strategy balances growth with risk management, maintaining a cash buffer.
balanced.read: This balanced approach aims for around 2.5% per month, focusing on risk-first growth. It reduces overall leverage and concentration while introducing a new, strong long setup. Expect moderate drawdowns and growth potential.

plan: Increase exposure to leveraged ETFs SOXL and SPAL to 6% each.
Add to METU, MUU, and PLTU to 6% each, leaning into tech/semis.
Trim SPY to 15% to free up capital for higher-conviction plays.

aggressive.read: This aggressive approach targets around 4% per month, aiming for stretched growth. It significantly increases exposure to leveraged ETFs and concentrates in high-scoring setups. Be aware of substantially higher drawdown potential and the daily decay/rebalancing of leveraged ETFs; strict stop discipline is crucial.

plan: Sell all high-beta single names like METU, MSFU, MUU, and PLTU to zero.
Exit all leveraged ETFs such as SOXL and SPAL for low drawdown.
Increase QQQI to 30% to prioritize steady monthly distributions.
This plan focuses on parking cash for yield and minimizing growth-oriented risk.
income.read: This income approach targets around 1% per month, prioritizing yield and low drawdown. It significantly reduces exposure to high-beta and leveraged assets, focusing on income-generating ETFs. Remember, distributions are variable, and NAV can still decline in market downturns.
